subject: Re: Quantization trade-study & evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Quantization trade-study & evals; next steps

Hi Alice / Tom;

Great to meet earlier; thanks for walking us through Acme's conversational support use case and the throughput targets (1k concurrent sessions, p95 latency < 400ms). Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

1) Model fit observations from call
- For short/interactive support dialogs, smaller instruction-tuned models in the 7B-13B range often hit better latency/cost trade-offs, but you flagged some long-context summarization tasks where the 70B family performs noticeably better on factuality.

2) Recommended eval plan (what we'll run next)
- Run a model-fit eval across three candidate families: Llama-2-13B-Chat (FP16 baseline), Llama-2-70B-Chat (FP16 baseline), and a Redwood-optimized 13B variant we discussed (mix of instruction tuning + safety filters).
- Quantization trade-study: evaluate AWQ (4-bit), GPTQ (4-bit), and FP8 (where supported) for each candidate to measure throughput vs. quality regressions.
- Metrics: ROUGE-L + custom exact-match and hallucination checks on your prompt set (please see attached acme_prompt_set_v1.txt).

3) Attachments & links
- I attached a quick seed eval we ran on similar support prompts (acme_quant_eval_results.csv) and a latency/throughput bench (model_latency_bench.pdf). Full eval artifacts will be shared to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=evals123

4) Next steps / asks
- Alice: can you confirm the final prompt set (attached) and add any additional long-context cases?
- Tom: is procurement comfortable sharing a standard NDA / SOW template so we can propose Dedicated capacity pricing?
- Internal (Dev / Michael): can you start the quantization bench runs on Dedicated dev pool and include AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 configs? Target: first pass results by EOD Monday (9/13).

I'll propose a short follow-up next week to review results and recommend a canary rollout plan (canary traffic, acceptance thresholds).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Quantization trade-study & evals; next steps

Great questions; short answers here, with a slightly longer technical note below.

TL;DR:
- AWQ (4-bit) usually gives the best throughput at low implementation complexity and often preserves subjective quality well for instruction-following; risk of subtle regressions exists and is workload-dependent.
- GPTQ (4-bit) can be slightly better for preserving FP16 behavior on some architectures but is more sensitive to calibration and can be slower to decode in some runtimes.
- FP8 gives near-FP16 quality in many cases and higher throughput where the runtime (and hardware) supports it, but availability depends on model compilation and infra (we can test).

Detailed notes (for your engineers):
- For short-turn conversation (Q&A, intent extraction), try AWQ on a 13B instruction-tuned model first; you'll likely meet p95 latency with good cost savings and minimal degradation.
- For long-context summarization where factuality matters, run the 70B family in parallel and compare hallucination metrics (we'll run a dedicated hallucination check that scores entity-level precision).
- Quantization bench plan: we'll produce per-model tables with tokens/sec (throughput), p50/p95 latency, and delta vs FP16 on key eval metrics (exact-match, rouge-l, hallucination-rate). Acceptance criteria example: max -3% absolute on ROUGE-L and <2% increase in hallucination-rate vs FP16 for canary pass.

Attachments: I added a short prompt-eval spec and a sample scoring script to Drive (see related links).

Dev / Michael: please include these columns in the bench CSV: model, config (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8), tokens_per_sec, p50_ms, p95_ms, rouge_l, exact_match, hallucination_rate. Start with the Redwood-optimized 13B and Llama-2-70B.

Marissa
